current.title: Tryptophan
current.line: Thanksgiving week: turkey takes the blame for tryptophan, but chicken and beef contain about as much of this amino acid.

weeks.title: Tryptophan
weeks.line: Thanksgiving week: turkey takes the blame for tryptophan, but chicken and beef contain about as much of this amino acid.

weeks.title: Benzoic acid
weeks.line: Cranberry sauce season: cranberries carry their own benzoic acid, the same preservative that is added to sodas and pickles.

weeks.title: Aspirin
weeks.line: Aspirin went on sale in 1899, but the idea is ancient: willow bark carries salicin, which the body turns into salicylic acid, the compound aspirin is made from.

weeks.title: Melatonin
weeks.line: Darker evenings are here: melatonin is the body's own nightfall signal, released as the light fades.

weeks.title: Sucrose
weeks.line: Trick-or-treat week: most Halloween candy is built on sucrose, the table sugar every other sweetener is measured against.

weeks.title: Adrenaline
weeks.line: Haunted-house season: a good scare releases adrenaline, the surge that readies the body for a burst of action.

weeks.title: β-Carotene
weeks.line: Leaf-peeping season: as leaves stop renewing their green chlorophyll, pigments like β-carotene show through as yellow and orange.

weeks.title: Americium
weeks.line: Fire Prevention Week: many home smoke alarms hold a speck of americium, a synthetic element whose radiation helps the alarm sense smoke.

weeks.title: Quinine
weeks.line: Tonic water gets its bitterness from quinine, which also makes the drink glow blue under a black light.

weeks.title: Cinnamaldehyde
weeks.line: Pumpkin spice has no pumpkin in it. It leads with cinnamon, and cinnamaldehyde is the molecule that makes cinnamon taste like cinnamon.
